display.purpose: The public site's hero headline only.

body.purpose: Workhorse prose, form labels, table content.

label.purpose: Section eyebrows, badges, IDs, status codes — intended mono, currently unwired (see DESIGN.md Typography gap).

accent.purpose: One rationed handwritten flourish on the public "tentang" page.

shadows.name: card-rest
shadows.purpose: The system's only default elevation — every card, everywhere, at rest.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus on buttons, inputs, and other interactive elements.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Buttons translate down 1px on :active — a quiet press acknowledgment, not a bounce.

motion.name: scroll-reveal
motion.value: linear both, animation-timeline: view(), animation-range: entry 5% cover 25%
motion.purpose: Marketing sections fade/slide up as they enter the viewport; disabled entirely under prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The default action button — a true capsule, Ledger Crimson fill.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 36px; padding: 0 12px; gap: 6px; border-radius: 26px; border: none; background: oklch(0.52 0.2 17); color: oklch(0.98 0.008 17); font-family: 'Public Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; transition: background 150ms ease, transform 150ms ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, oklch(0.52 0.2 17) 80%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgb(112 4 34 / 0.3); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: The one button variant that keeps a visible border at rest.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 36px; padding: 0 12px; border-radius: 26px; border: 1px solid oklch(0.92 0.004 286.32); background: oklch(1 0 0); color: oklch(0.141 0.005 285.823); font-family: 'Public Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; transition: background 150ms ease; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: oklch(0.967 0.001 286.375); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgb(112 4 34 / 0.3); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Borderless at rest; the ring only appears on focus.
components.css: .ds-input { height: 36px; width: 100%; padding: 4px 12px; border-radius: 22px; border: 1px solid transparent; background: color-mix(in oklch, oklch(0.92 0.004 286.32) 50%, transparent); color: oklch(0.141 0.005 285.823); font-family: 'Public Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; outline: none; transition: border-color 150ms ease, box-shadow 150ms ease; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: oklch(0.552 0.016 285.938); } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: oklch(0.7 0.012 17); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgb(112 4 34 / 0.3); }

components.name: Default Badge
components.description: Capsule status/category tag; swap background+text per the semantic color family in use.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 20px; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 22px; background: oklch(0.58 0.2 25); color: white; font-family: 'Public Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; }

narrative.overview: KAMMI ID keeps the national record of a youth organization: who its cadres are, what they've earned, which structures they belong to. A ledger has to be exact — but this one refuses to feel like an interrogation. Every surface that touches data leans on precise, monospace-coded numbers and IDs; every surface the user touches directly (buttons, inputs, badges) is soft-edged, almost capsule-shaped, with no border standing guard until the user actually needs one. The result reads as rigorous without being cold: an archive that keeps its promises about accuracy while refusing the visual language of a government form. This system explicitly rejects the "Government App" aesthetic — rigid rectangles, defensive borders on every field, blue-grey monotony, and interfaces that make the user prove their intentions before they're allowed to act. The Kindly Ledger trusts first: surfaces stay quiet and unbordered until interaction actually calls for structure.
keyCharacteristics: Soft-edged, unguarded: buttons and badges round all the way to a capsule; inputs and cards carry no visible border at rest, only a whisper of shadow and ring.
Precision where it counts: IDs, dates, and counts are set in a distinct label/mono voice, separate from the conversational body text.
One human accent: a handwritten typeface appears exactly once, on the public "tentang" (about) page — a deliberate, rationed warmth, not a system-wide habit.
One loud color: Ledger Crimson is the system's only high-chroma accent for actions and identity; everything else is neutral or semantically coded (status, jenjang, gender).

rules.name: The Rare Accent Rule
rules.body: Ledger Crimson appears on primary actions, active states, and identity marks — nowhere else. If a screen needs a second strong color, reach for the semantic system instead of a second shade of crimson.

rules.name: The One Family, One Hue Rule
rules.body: A given semantic family (Jenjang, gender, Struktur type, Keadaan) never reuses a hue within itself, but hues do repeat across families when the underlying meaning is genuinely related. Don't invent a new hue for a new category without checking whether an existing family already owns the meaning.

rules.name: The Unguarded Rule
rules.body: No interactive element (button, input, badge) carries a visible border at rest. A border or heavy ring appearing on an unfocused, valid, non-hovered element is a bug, not a style choice.

rules.name: The Capsule Rule
rules.body: The radius scale is deliberately used at its top end for anything the user touches directly: buttons and badges clamp into true capsules; inputs get rounded-3xl; cards get rounded-4xl at a much larger box, reading as generously softened rather than literally round.

dos: Do reserve Ledger Crimson for actions and identity — semantic color (Jenjang, gender, Struktur type, Keadaan) carries everything else.
Do keep interactive elements borderless at rest; let focus/error states be the only time a border or heavy ring appears.
Do use the top of the radius scale (3xl/4xl) for anything the user directly touches (buttons, badges, inputs, cards).
Do treat the handwritten accent (Caveat) as a single, rationed flourish — not a typeface to reach for generally.
Do pick Dialog for confirmations/short actions and Sheet for a primary create/edit flow, per the observed split.
donts: Don't use the "Government App" aesthetic: sharp rectangular corners, defensive borders on every field, monotonous blue-grey neutrals, or interfaces that force the user to justify an action before they can take it.
Don't introduce a second high-chroma accent color into primary UI — route it through the semantic system instead.
Don't assume font-geist-mono is rendering as monospace until the implementation gap is closed; don't design new UI that depends on it looking different from body text.
Don't invent a new hue for a new categorical badge without checking whether an existing semantic family already owns that meaning.
Don't use gradient text or fills inside the dashboard/data surfaces — gradients exist on the public marketing site's hero-adjacent sections only.
